title: Week 31
subtitle: The baby is practicing breathing, and you are probably practicing patience.

baby.size: About the size of a coconut
baby.development: The baby is practicing breathing movements with amniotic fluid. All five senses are working. The pupils can react to light. Most babies turn head-down around now, though there is still time.

you.body: Your uterus is about four and a half inches above your belly button. You may have more pressure low down, more frequent urination, and more trouble getting comfortable. Colostrum may start to leak.
you.mind: You may start to feel ready and unready at the same time. That is not a contradiction — it is what the last two months are like.

coreActions.title: Pack the bag and leave it by the door
coreActions.why: Labor does not wait for you to find the charger. A packed bag is the one thing you can control about a day you cannot schedule.
coreActions.detail: For you: ID, insurance card, a long phone cable, comfortable clothes, a robe, slippers, toiletries, snacks, and a going-home outfit. For the baby: a going-home outfit, a hat, and a blanket. For your support person: clothes, snacks, cash for parking, and their own charger. Put the car seat in the car now, not later.

options.label: The hospital's list
options.detail: Short and accurate for that hospital.

options.label: Ten things, nothing more
options.detail: The hospital has most of it. Travel light.

coreActions.skipIf: The bag is packed and in the car.

coreActions.title: Review your birth preferences with your support person
coreActions.why: The person with you in labor will speak for you at the moments you cannot. They need to know what matters before, not during.
coreActions.detail: Walk through each preference and say why it matters. Agree on what happens if you cannot decide. Give them a copy and put one in your chart. Keep it to one page — a long list is harder to follow under pressure.

options.label: Talk it through at home
options.detail: Twenty minutes, one page, two copies.

options.label: Bring it to your next visit
options.detail: Ask your OB to put it in the chart.

coreActions.skipIf: You have no support person, or the plan is already shared.

coreActions.title: Know what colostrum is
coreActions.why: It is what you make first, and it is not a small amount of milk — it is a different food, in small amounts, which is what a newborn stomach holds.
coreActions.detail: Colostrum is thick and yellow and comes in teaspoons, not ounces. A newborn's stomach is about the size of a cherry on day one. Feeding often in the first days is what brings your milk in. If you plan to formula feed, none of this changes what you do — it is just what your body is doing.

options.label: Ask a lactation consultant
options.detail: Most hospitals have one. Free while you are there.

coreActions.skipIf: You already know, or you are not breastfeeding.

alsoKnow.title: Most babies turn by 36 weeks
alsoKnow.body: There is still room to turn. If the baby is breech at 36 weeks, your OB will talk through options, including a version. That conversation can wait until then.

alsoKnow.title: More bathroom trips is pressure, not a problem
alsoKnow.body: The head pressing on the bladder is why. It eases if the baby drops, then comes back. Call if it burns or comes with fever.

alsoKnow.title: Know the hospital entrance before the day
alsoKnow.body: Drive the route once. Find the labor and delivery entrance, not the main one. Ask where to park at 2am. It is a small thing that removes a real panic.

redFlags.text: A clear change in your baby's usual movement
Fluid that keeps leaking, or any vaginal bleeding

appointments.label: Prenatal visit
appointments.note: Every two weeks. Ask about the baby's position.

sources.title: How to Tell When Labor Begins
